subject: Linguistics
title: The Indo-European Family
description: A fast breakdown of The Indo-European Family for builders.

hook.text: English, Hindi, Greek, and Persian are all cousins—descended from one language spoken 6,000 years ago.

buildup.text: Indo-European is the largest language family, with over three billion native speakers.

discovery.text: William Jones noticed in 1786 that Sanskrit, Greek, and Latin were too similar to be coincidence.

twist.text: The original Proto-Indo-European language was never written down—we've reconstructed it from its descendants.

climax.text: Ten major branches—Germanic, Romance, Slavic, Indo-Iranian, Celtic, and more—all trace back to one source.

punchline.text: Three billion people speak dialects of one ancient language.

quiz.question: Who first observed the connection between Sanskrit, Greek, and Latin?
